newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-CZECH GOVERNMENT PLEDGES SUPPORT FOR EURO 2004 JOINT BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CZECH GOVERNMENT PLEDGES SUPPORT FOR EURO 2004 JOINT BID.

text.p: The Czech government has pledged its support for a possible joint bid for the 2004 European soccer championship finals with Austria.

Press officials for Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus confirmed on Friday that Klaus has met Czech Football Association Chairman Frantisek Chvalovsky and his Austrian counterpart Beppo Mauhart to hear their joint bid proposal.
Klaus, an avid supporter of Czech soccer, pledged the Czech government's full support -- seen as necessary for the bid's success -- for the plan, officials said.
No mention was made of how much, if any, financial support the Czech government might give.
Mauhart is also reported to be negotiating with soccer federations in Switzerland, Hungary, and Croatia on the possibility of co-hosting the tournament.
Spain is likely to figure high among bidders for the 2004 championship. UEFA is expected to decide on the venue in 1998.
In the year 2000, Belgium and the Netherlands will become the first joint hosts for the tournament.
